question: Which one of the following river marks the eastern-most boundary of the Himalayas?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Brahmaputra**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Brahmaputra** river marks the **eastern-most boundary of the Himalayas**.
 
• The river **originates from the Angsi Glacier in Tibet**, where it is known as the **Yarlung Tsangpo River**.
 
• It flows across southern Tibet to break through the Himalayas in great gorges and into** Arunachal Pradesh** (India), where it is known as the **Dihang**.
 
• From Arunachal Pradesh, it flows southwest through the Assam Valley as Brahmaputra and south through Bangladesh as the Jamuna.
 
• The river is crucial for the ecosystems and the livelihoods of millions of people in the regions it flows through.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Ganga** river is one of the major rivers in India but does not mark the eastern boundary of the Himalayas.
 
• The **Godavari** river is the **second longest river in India** but is located in central India.
 
• The **Chambal** river is a **tributary of the Yamuna** river in central India.
 
• The **Brahmaputra **river has a total **length **of about** 2,900 km **(1,800 mi) and is one of the major rivers of the world in terms of discharge and sediment transport.
